concerns.text: The plan defers power analysis (`[deferred] – script will compute post‑hoc power`). Without an a priori power calculation, the study may be under‑powered to detect the expected effects of nesting depth and branching factor, jeopardizing the validity of any conclusions.

Cox proportional‑hazards models assume proportional hazards over time, yet the plan does not include any test (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals) or alternative modeling if the assumption is violated. This threatens the causal interpretability of the hazard ratios.

The design controls only topological metrics (depth, branching) but does not account for other potential confounds such as natural‑language complexity, token length, or semantic difficulty of the puzzles, which could also influence convergence speed.

Success is defined as `path_coverage ≥ 0.95` **and** final state matches ground truth. Relying on a coverage threshold may not fully capture logical correctness; small mismatches could still satisfy the threshold, leading to false‑positive success labels.
The extended‑budget run is performed on a 20 % subset of the data. Analyzing convergence on a non‑representative subset can bias the estimated budget‑exhaustion rate and limit generalizability.
